This is the Lab Week 10 document for R-DAVIS. Complete the tasks below in this file (or in your own `.Rmd` or `.R` file, if you prefer), save it, and upload that file to Canvas. No need to render it to HTML.

In this assignment, you'll use for loops, `lapply()`, and `sapply()` on the California wildfire air-quality data from lecture. Each row is one place on one day, 2006–2020. `pm10` and `ozone` are the total daily concentrations, and `pm10_fire` and `ozone_fire` are the parts that came from wildfire smoke.

Load the data:

```{r wk10a}
# data at https://ucd-rdavis.github.io/R-DAVIS/data/ca_wildfire_air.csv

```

1) Not everything needs a loop. Add a column called `ozone_other` to `air` that holds the ozone that did *not* come from wildfire smoke (`ozone` minus `ozone_fire`). In a sentence, explain why you don't need a for loop or `lapply()` for this.

2) Use a for loop to find the highest `ozone_fire` value in each city. Store the answers in a vector that you make *before* the loop, then print the vector. Check your answer with `group_by()` and `summarise()`.

3) Use `sapply()` with a function written inside it (`function(x) ...`) to count, for each of the columns `pm10`, `pm10_fire`, `ozone`, and `ozone_fire`, the number of days on which that column was above its own mean.

4) Write a function called `year_summary(data, yr)` that returns a one-row tibble for a single year with three columns: `year`, `smoke_days` (the number of rows across all six places with `pm10_fire > 0`), and `worst_city` (the city with the highest `pm10_fire` that year). Test it on 2018. Then use `lapply()` and `bind_rows()` to make a table with one row for each year from 2006 to 2020. Which year had the most smoke days?

5) Use `split()` to split `air` into one data frame per city. Then use `lapply()` with a function written inside it to compare air quality on smoke days and other days. For each city, return a one-row tibble with the city name, the mean `pm10` on smoke days (`pm10_fire > 0`), and the mean `pm10` on all other days. Stack the results with `bind_rows()`. In which city is the difference largest?
